hypotheses.justification: This follows from hφ. IsLocalRing supplies Nontrivial A, and LinearMap.charpoly_natDegree identifies the characteristic polynomial's natural degree with finrank A V. Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_mul and Polynomial.natDegree_X_sub_C show that the right-hand side of hφ has natural degree 2. Derive h2 this way and use the existing proof.

A direct coordinate argument avoids locality. If A is trivial, Module.subsingleton makes V trivial, so the conclusion holds. Otherwise choose a basis b indexed by Fin 2 using h2, and put ψ = φ - β • 1. The characteristic-polynomial identity gives trace φ = α + β, hence trace ψ = α - β, using charpoly_eq_of_finrank_eq_two and eq_of_quadratic_eq. By hw choose c₀,c₁ with ψ(b i) = cᵢ • w. Writing w = x₀ • b 0 + x₁ • b 1, the matrix trace formula gives c₀*x₀ + c₁*x₁ = α - β. Consequently ψ(w) = (α - β) • w, so ordProj_apply and hu give ordProj φ α β w = w. Thus A ∙ w is contained in the range; the reverse inclusion is exactly the existing argument using hw. This also covers w = 0 without cancellation.
